entities.summary: Abraham van Diepenbeeck was a Dutch painter, draftsman, glass painter, print maker and tapestry designer who worked most of his active career in Antwerp. He designed glass windows for various churches and monasteries in Antwerp for which he made many design drawings and oil sketches. He engraved and designed many prints which were published by prominent Antwerp printers such as van Meurs, the Plantin Press and Martinus van den Enden the Elder. He had a close relationship with the workshop of the leading Flemish Baroque painter Peter Paul Rubens and collaborated on various projects under the direction of Rubens.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Abraham van Diepenbeeck's designs for glass windows and prints had a significant regional impact in Antwerp during the Early Modern era, influencing the development of Baroque art. His collaborations with Peter Paul Rubens further solidified his reputation as a prominent artist.
